explanation: Hooke's law says an ideal spring exerts a restoring force F = k x proportional to its displacement x from equilibrium, where k (N/m) is the spring constant; the force points back toward equilibrium. The elastic potential energy stored is the area under that F-vs-x line, PE = 1/2 k x^2, which grows quadratically. On the AP exam this pairing is key: F is linear in x (used in SHM, F = -k x) while stored energy is quadratic in x. The animation stretches a spring while showing the restoring-force arrow grow linearly and a dot climbing the 1/2 k x^2 energy parabola.
bullets: Restoring force F = k x is LINEAR — the arrow length scales with stretch x.
Stored energy PE = 1/2 k x^2 is the triangular area under the F-x line.
Stiffer springs (larger k) give both more force and more stored energy.
A negative-x compression stores the same energy as the equal +x stretch.
